title: Copper Scroll research methods and results
scope: Research approaches in the Copper Scroll Experimental Approaches dossier (23 October 2026), reconciled with recorded project results through 30 October 2026. This record covers site-finding research; it does not schedule unfinished methods.
priority_rule: Choose a method only for its ability to change a candidate identification, candidate set, reading or geographic interpretation. IDs preserve the research proposals' original numbering and do not give priority.

methods.title: AI extraction from excavation reports
methods.result: Mechanical checks passed on 50 reports. Two-model agreement is not an accuracy estimate; the hand-coded answer key was dropped on 24 October.
methods.remaining: Use existing rows provisionally. A bounded independently checked sample would be needed for an accuracy claim; do not resume hand-coding as an inherited task.
methods.effect: Provisional extraction can help locate reports; it does not validate candidate dates or feature identities.

methods.title: AI on pre-development imagery
methods.state: Resolution gate passed on one frame
methods.result: HEXAGON 1978 resolves large open Qumran pools; CORONA 1967 did not resolve the eight tested pools. The blind marking rule also marks ordinary rooms.
methods.remaining: A detector on unseen ground and pre-development RAF imagery have not been validated by that test. Original RAF scans remain a dependency.
methods.effect: Supports inspection of open features around four metres and larger on the tested film; it establishes no buried-feature detection or new site.

methods.title: Thermal and photogrammetric drone survey
methods.result: The 23 October Experimental Approaches dossier proposes comparing ground-discovered openings with ordinary imagery. No completed test of the additional detection value of thermal imaging was found in the reviewed results.
methods.remaining: Israel Antiquities Authority survey records must first show a consequential detection gap; a partner-led flight depends on that result and appropriate access.
methods.effect: Assess added detection value before treating a new survey as useful.

methods.title: A search-theory map
methods.result: The project already has coverage and search-effectiveness analyses. The proposed pre-2017 prediction test against later cave finds has no recorded result in the reviewed material.
methods.remaining: Requires dated search footprints, survey outcomes and defensible detection rates. Existing speculative weights cannot supply a calibrated map.
methods.effect: A map is worthwhile only if it changes a real choice and survives a comparison with a simpler baseline.

methods.title: Muon imaging
methods.result: No project-specific void-detectability simulation or field result is recorded in the reviewed material.
methods.remaining: A named target with detector access below it, plus a partner simulation of signal and run time.
methods.effect: Keep as a conditional technique; no detector campaign follows from the dossier's precedent alone.

methods.title: Dating the installations
methods.state: Source work done; sampling pilot unrun
methods.result: The project has evaluated construction phases and plaster-dating literature. The proposed five-fragment screening pilot has no recorded result.
methods.remaining: A date-bearing construction contact that would decide a consequential candidate claim, suitable material and a licensed sampling partner.
methods.effect: Dating a repair or unrelated plaster cannot settle the original installation's age.

methods.title: Imaging both faces of the strips
methods.state: New photographs received; new imaging unrun
methods.result: The University of Southern California supplied 93 colour photographs of the front (recto). Public previews of front and back (verso) photographs also exist; back photography is therefore not an untested idea.
methods.remaining: New 3D or reflectance imaging of the original backs remains a separate proposal. Determine whether existing photographs leave a specific consequential observation unavailable.
methods.effect: Image arrival and a new imaging campaign are different achievements; study access does not grant publication permission.

methods.title: Computational re-reading
methods.result: Registration of 1988 and 1994 photographs reached median errors of 0.12–0.19 mm on tested segments. Matching to the early plates in Discoveries in the Judaean Desert, volume III, failed the acceptance test and stopped. Recent colour-photo readings remain exploratory; several words are lost or unreadable.
methods.remaining: A distinct better observation or calibrated fresh-reader test must justify reopening a specific reading. The column XII, line 10 (column 12, line 10) images are exposed to earlier atlas users.
methods.effect: Do not count registration accuracy, a tentative letter lean or an exposed reading as an independently confirmed location.

methods.title: Unidentified fragments and the explanatory copy
methods.result: No completed known-join recovery test or identification of an explanatory-copy fragment is recorded in the reviewed material.
methods.remaining: A fixed distinctive-text query and a test on known fragment joins at realistic fragment sizes, with a chance baseline and suitable corpus access.
methods.effect: This remains a long-shot hypothesis. Common-word matches cannot establish that a second copy existed.

methods.title: The hoard check
methods.result: Under the registered default talent reading, 0/45 sums matched; under the 71 g karsh reading, 27/30 matched. Milik's alternative numeral at VIII 9 leaves a talent exception. Thirteen hoards supply the karsh matches.
methods.remaining: Precise findspot, depth and container records would be needed for a discriminating comparison; the weight screen should not be rerun without a correction.
methods.effect: The smaller unit is compatible with known hoard sizes. Weight alone identifies no scroll deposit.

methods.title: Forecasting and blind panels
methods.result: A reading protocol and letter controls exist. No completed human-epigrapher panel or forecasting tournament is recorded in the reviewed results.
methods.remaining: Choose a question whose answer can resolve, arrange qualified independent readers and appropriate image rights, and record prior exposure.
methods.effect: A panel can clarify disagreement; a tournament needs enough resolvable questions to justify its overhead.
